subject: Finalizing MAP: production bridge & capacity activation timeline
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@edgehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + proposed activation window for Dedicated capacity

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan that aligns the evaluation milestones to the capacity reservation and activation steps you asked about. High-level items in the PDF:

- Evaluation runbook (3-week cadence: smoke tests, perf sweep, latency SLO verification)
- Acceptance gates tied to traffic profiles (P50/P95 targets)
- Capacity reservation: initial GPU pool (8 x A100-equivalent or quantized MLC equivalents) with runway to scale to 24 devices in two tranches
- Lead times: estimated procurement/placement for Dedicated pockets (12–16 weeks), Private on-prem timing varies by network approvals (~18–26 weeks)
- Key owners and dependencies (procurement, security review, SOC2 evidence)

Next steps I suggest:
1) You review draft MAP and confirm acceptance gates that match EdgeHealth QA (I highlighted the ones I think will be sticky).
2) Procurement to confirm target commit window (we recommended July 15–22 to trigger the first tranche).
3) We schedule a technical acceptance run (we can reserve a short pilot node during evaluation to reduce risk).

Attached: EdgeHealth_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (MAP + milestone checklist).

If you want, Marissa can schedule a 30-min MAP walkthrough this week — she’s on Cc.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

Attachment: EdgeHealth_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 420KB)
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@edgehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>, EdgeHealth Procurement <procurement@edgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + proposed activation window for Dedicated capacity

Logan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear milestones. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we lock dates:

1) Can you confirm the assumptions behind the 12–16 week Dedicated lead time? Is that tied to specific GPU SKUs or to a generic Dedicated pool allocation?
2) For the initial pool of 8 devices, what throughput do you recommend for our live inference baseline (we’re expecting ~800 concurrent inference sessions at peak for v1)?
3) Our procurement lead (Tom) wants to understand billing/commit phasing — do we have a per-tranche discount schedule or incentives for earlier commit?

Also — we’ll need SOC2 evidence and a short security questionnaire filled out for our GRC team. Procurement copied.

Regards,
Sarah Lin
Head of ML Platforms | EdgeHealth
<sarah.lin@edgehealth.com>

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@edgehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + proposed activation window for Dedicated capacity

Sarah / Tom —

Thanks — great questions. I’ll answer inline and attach a short sizing worksheet.

1) Lead time assumptions: the 12–16 week window is conservative and assumes Dedicated pockets provisioned in our US-west region using NVIDIA A100-class hardware. If you accept a quantized MLC (8-bit) profile we can often shorten practical lead time by ~2–3 weeks because those instances are more flexibly allocated across our fleet. The MAP has a note on acceptable model quantization profiles.

2) Throughput for 8-device pool: for your profile (~800 concurrent inference sessions, average request length ~180 tokens, tail P95 latency target 250ms) we recommend starting with 8 devices configured with continuous batching and a KV prefix cache for stable prompts. This should sustain ~600–900 concurrent sessions depending on request concurrency characteristics. I attached GPU_Pool_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx with baseline numbers. We can size up to 24 devices for peak headroom and model ensemble scenarios.

3) Billing / commit phasing: we offer tranche-based pricing — initial tranche commit (first 8 devices) is charged at standard reserved rate; second tranche (next 8) comes with a 7.5% committed discount if signed within 90 days of the first tranche activation, third tranche (final 8) gets 12% if signed within 120 days. I attached MAP_SLA_Draft.pdf that includes a pricing appendix.

Security & SOC2: Marissa will coordinate SOC2 artifacts and our compliance pack (we can share a time-limited evidence bundle and a small-attendance audit session).

Next actions proposed:
- Procurement: confirm whether July 15–22 works as an internal approval window.
- EdgeHealth: confirm acceptance gates (I’ve highlighted the two acceptance tests I expect will be the largest blockers).
- Redwood: we’ll provision a pilot node for a 7-day acceptance run starting immediately after your QA signoff.

I’m happy to hop on a quick call if you want to run through the sizing worksheet together.

Thanks,
Logan

Attachments: MAP_SLA_Draft.pdf (PDF, 180KB); GPU_Pool_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx (XLSX, 78KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@edgehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + proposed activation window for Dedicated capacity

Sarah —

Quick technical note from infra: we can shorten the hardware placement part of the timeline if EdgeHealth can accept the following mitigations during the first tranche pilot:

- Use quantized model profiles (8-bit per token) for the smoke/perf sweep — reduces memory pressure and increases placement flexibility.
- Allow a short burst window (up to 80% of peak) during the first 10 business days of pilot — gives us operational headroom while you validate latency.

On lead times: the 12–16 week number integrates logistics (firmware validation, rack allocation, network ACLs for Dedicated pockets). If procurement can pre-clear network ACLs and we get SOC2 evidence in parallel, we typically see the practical window slip toward the 10–12 week side.

I’ve pasted the relevant excerpt from the MAP under our acceptance gates section to make it explicit: 

> Acceptance Gate 2 — Performance & Scale
> - P95 latency <= 250ms on 99th percentile of test runs
> - Successful KV cache warmups showing >= 30% reduction in per-token compute cost
>
If you’re comfortable with the mitigations above, we’ll mark the MAP milestone to trigger provisioning on July 20.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + proposed activation window for Dedicated capacity

Logan / Karthik / team —

Thanks for the clarifications. Procurement and GRC reviewed the MAP and the SOC2 evidence plan — all good on our side provided the following two conditions are met:

1) We receive the completed SOC2 artifact bundle (time-limited access) by July 8 so our security team can sign off.
2) The DocuSign for tranche 1 is issued on July 12 so we can target an internal approval sprint the week of July 15.

EdgeHealth accepts the quantized-profile mitigation for the pilot; we’d like the burst window limited to the first 5 business days instead of 10 — will that be a hard blocker operationally?

If you can confirm those two items and share the DocuSign link, we’ll proceed to finalize. I’ve looped Ben from Redwood’s pricing team for any last-minute tranche discount clarifications.

Tom Alvarez
Senior Procurement Manager | EdgeHealth
procurement@edgehealth.com
